title: Digitalization project: Identification of cardiovascular risk patients and detection of advanced liver fibrosis in patients with type-2-diabetes using non-invasive scores in outpatient care in Hessen
summary:
Diabetes mellitus type 2 is a very common metabolic disorder worldwide and can lead to damage to blood vessels and various organ systems. The coexistence of diabetes and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease has received less attention and is also underdiagnosed. Recent studies have found non-alcoholic fatty liver disease in up to 70% of patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Fatty liver disease increases the risk of cardiovascular and kidney disease and can progress to liver fibrosis ("scarring") and cirrhosis ("shrunken liver") with serious complications (including liver cancer). Therefore, it is important to detect fatty liver disease and its complications as early as possible and to initiate appropriate treatment and monitoring.
Using special medical scoring systems, the risk of fatty liver disease or advanced liver disease can be determined based on a small amount of data (e.g., age, BMI, waist circumference, results from routine blood tests). As part of the study, the above-mentioned scores will be collected in diabetes-oriented practices and transmitted via a digital interface to the Liver Center at Frankfurt University Hospital. In the case of an abnormal score, patients will be offered further diagnostic testing according to current recommendations and guidelines from professional societies.
These data will provide insights into the prevalence of fatty liver disease and its advanced stages in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The project will investigate the application of simple, noninvasive scores for timely diagnosis and treatment of these diseases, as well as the effects of digitally connecting outpatient diabetes centers with a hepatology center, such as the one at Frankfurt University Hospital. The results are expected to improve the quality of treatment for future patients.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Unselected patients (age >=18 years) with diabetes mellitus type 2 from five diabetes specialist practices in Hessen.
Informed consent  for participation.
Exclusion criteria:
Known advanced liver disease (fibrosis ≥3, liver cirrhosis, HCC) in patients with diabetes mellitus type 2.
Pregnancy.
No informed consent.
